text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD
- Brussels is likely to give the green light to the sale of Creditanstalt to Bank Austria. A final decision may come in the middle of March.
- Chancellor Viktor Klima, speaking in an emergency parliamentary debate, warned against simple solutions to unemployment. He wants to bolster Austrian export industry
- What should have been a formal vote on Herbert Tumpel as new Chamber of Labour chief failed on a technicality
- The conservative People's Party wants to review its previously amicable relationship with Albanian President Sali Berisha.
- Harmony and unity in the coalition government during a parliamentary debate on unemployment. Strong criticism from the opposition.
- Ankerbrot takeover by Germany's Mueller now certain.
- Former Social Affairs Minister Franz Hums will also step down from his job in the rail union
DIE PRESSE
- Agreement on flexible working hours: the coalition celebrates but the opposition is unhappy
- Chancellor Klima does not want to commit Austria too early to an international security body
- January year-on-year inflation fell to 1.9 percent from 2.3 percent in December
- Coalition pins its hopes for reducing unemployment on exports, new technology and education
- The metal industry will be among the first to introduce flexible working
KURIER
- Flexible working. Employees' income will fall by 10 billion schillings
- The government has reached agreement on regulating regional radio and cable and satellite tv. By the autumn there could be 10 regional and 45 local private radio stations
- Flexible working. The exchange of money for security
- Brussels is sending a final warning to Austria, ordering it to do away with anonymous savings accounts
- Bawag's interest in post office savings bank PSG grows
